items.title: 6.2.4 Position of a Point with Respect to a Circle (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 176: 6.2.4 Theorem 1 (outside, on, inside) with Proof and Figure 6.8; Example 11

blocks.text: Kabhi kabhi sawal yeh hota hai ke koi diya hua point circle ke bahar hai, circle par hai, ya andar. Figure bana kar andaza lagana aasan lagta hai, magar jab point circle ke bilkul qareeb ho to aankh dhoka de jati hai. Is sabaq mein ek aisa test seekhenge jo sirf ek substitution se pakka jawab deta hai. Aage 6.2.6 mein bhi yahi baat kaam aayegi, jab hum dekhenge ke kisi point se kitne tangents kheenche ja sakte hain.

Theorem 1: Point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) circle
\[x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\]
ke bahar, circle par, ya andar hota hai, is hisaab se ke
\[x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c \gtreqless 0\]

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par magenta circle, centre C(-g, -f). Teen points P(x1, y1) cyan lines se centre se jure hain: ek circle ke bahar (upar baayen), ek circle par (daayen) aur ek andar (centre ke neeche).
blocks.caption: Figure 6.8: A point P(x1, y1) outside, on and inside the circle with centre C(-g, -f) (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.8)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Nishan \(\gtreqless\) ko tarteeb se parhiye: \(>\) ka jor "bahar" se, \(=\) ka "circle par" se, aur \(<\) ka "andar" se. Yani theorem ki ek line asal mein teen baatein keh rahi hai. Figure 6.8 mein teeno points ko centre se jora gaya hai; bahar wale ka faasla radius se zyada, circle wale ka barabar, aur andar wale ka kam hai.

Saboot (Proof): circle ka centre \(C(-g, -f)\) aur radius \(r = \sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\) hai. Point \(P(x_{1}, y_{1})\) bahar, circle par ya andar hoga, is hisaab se ke
\[|CP| > r, \quad |CP| = r, \quad \text{ya} \quad |CP| < r,\]
yani \(|CP| \gtreqless r\). Distance formula se \(|CP|\) likhein:
\[\sqrt{(x_{1} + g)^{2} + (y_{1} + f)^{2}} \gtreqless \sqrt{g^{2} + f^{2} - c}\]
Dono sides ka square lete hain (kyun ke sab quantities non-negative hain, square karne se inequality ka rukh nahin badalta):
\[(x_{1} + g)^{2} + (y_{1} + f)^{2} \gtreqless g^{2} + f^{2} - c\]
Brackets kholiye:
\[x_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + g^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2fy_{1} + f^{2}\]
\[\gtreqless g^{2} + f^{2} - c\]
\(g^{2}\) aur \(f^{2}\) dono taraf hain, cancel kar dein:
\[x_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + y_{1}^{2} + 2fy_{1} \gtreqless -c\]
\(-c\) ko left par le aayein. Is tarah:
\[x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c \gtreqless 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is proof mein do chhoti baatein kaam kar rahi hain:
1. Hum faaslon (distances) ka muqabla kar rahe hain, aur faasla kabhi negative nahin hota. Isi liye square karne se \(>\), \(=\), \(<\) waise ke waise rehte hain. (Negative numbers mein yeh zaroori nahin: \(-3 < 2\) magar \(9 > 4\).)
2. Cancel karne ke baad left side minus right side asal mein \(|CP|^{2} - r^{2}\) hai. Yani number \(S_{1} = x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c\) dar-asal \(|CP|^{2} - r^{2}\) hai, aur us ka sign batata hai ke \(P\) kahan hai.
Zaroori shart: substitute karne se pehle \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 hone chahiye. Agar \(2x^{2} + 2y^{2} + \ldots\) ho to pehle 2 se taqseem kar lein (waise positive number se taqseem sign nahin badalti, magar 6.2.7 mein length nikalte waqt yeh zaroori hoga).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin. Circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 25\) aur teen points lijiye:
\((6, 0)\): \(36 - 25 = 11 > 0\), bahar.
\((3, 4)\): \(9 + 16 - 25 = 0\), circle par.
\((1, 2)\): \(1 + 4 - 25 = -20 < 0\), andar.
Figure se bhi yahi nazar aata hai: radius 5 hai, aur origin se in points ke faasle 6, 5 aur \(\sqrt{5}\) hain.
Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain. Is mein sirf ek substitution hai, lekin signs ka khayal rakhna zaroori hai, kyun ke circle mein \(-3y\) aur \(-10\) jaise negative terms hain.

blocks.title: Example 11
blocks.problem: Determine whether the point \(P(2, 3)\) lies outside, on, or inside the circle: \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x - 3y - 10 = 0\)
steps:
Diya gaya: point \(P(2, 3)\) aur circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x - 3y - 10 = 0\).
Maloom karna: \(P\) circle ke bahar hai, circle par hai ya andar.
Tareeqa: Theorem 1. Point ke coordinates circle ki equation ke left-hand side mein rakhenge (yahan \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients pehle hi 1 hain, is liye taqseem ki zaroorat nahin) aur jawab ka sign dekhenge: positive to bahar, zero to circle par, negative to andar.

Qadam 1: \(x = 2\), \(y = 3\) left-hand side mein rakhna
\[(2)^{2} + (3)^{2} + 2(2) - 3(3) - 10\]
\[= 4 + 9 + 4 - 9 - 10\]
\[= -2 < 0\]
Kyun: Theorem 1 kehta hai ke \(x_{1}^{2} + y_{1}^{2} + 2gx_{1} + 2fy_{1} + c\) ka sign hi faisla karta hai. Dhyan dein: \(-3(3) = -9\), sign ka khayal rakhiye.

Qadam 2: Nateeja
Value negative hai, is liye point circle ke andar hai.
Kyun: negative ka matlab hai \(|CP|^{2} < r^{2}\), yani \(P\) centre se radius se kam faasle par hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(2g = 2\), \(2f = -3\), to centre \(C\left(-1, \frac{3}{2}\right)\) aur
\[r^{2} = 1 + \dfrac{9}{4} + 10 = \dfrac{53}{4}\]
\[|CP|^{2} = 3^{2} + \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{45}{4}\]
\(\frac{45}{4} < \frac{53}{4}\); aur farq \(\frac{45}{4} - \frac{53}{4} = -2\) bilkul wahi value hai jo Qadam 1 mein aayi. Theorem ka asal matlab yahi hai: woh value \(|CP|^{2} - r^{2}\) hai.
blocks.answer: \(4 + 9 + 4 - 9 - 10 = -2 < 0\); is liye point \(P(2, 3)\) circle ke andar hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) ko circle ki equation ke left side mein rakhiye (\(x^{2}\), \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients 1 hon).
2. Positive: bahar. Zero: circle par. Negative: andar.
3. Yeh value asal mein \(|CP|^{2} - r^{2}\) hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Signs ulat dena: positive ka matlab bahar hai, andar nahin.
2. Aisi equation mein substitute karna jis mein \(x^{2}\), \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients negative hon (maslan terms idhar udhar karne ke baad). Pehle circle ko \(x^{2} + y^{2} + \ldots = 0\) ki shakal mein likhiye.
3. \(-3y\) jaise negative coefficients mein hisaab ki ghalti.
